subject.title: WhatsApp inter_session delivery requests can be wrongly suppressed as REPLY_SKIP / ANNOUNCE_SKIP / NO_REPLY

question: Should this WhatsApp explicit-delivery symptom be fixed by a narrow `sessions_send` source-reply prompt/runtime repair now, folded into the broader structured handoff contract, or delegated to the open requester-return-path PR after its blockers are resolved?
rationale: The remaining fix changes model-facing inter-session delivery semantics and overlaps both an open PR and broader A2A handoff API work, so automation should not choose the permanent contract alone.

options.title: Keep as WhatsApp acceptance work
options.body: Keep this issue open until a narrow PR or repaired successor proves explicit WhatsApp source replies are delivered without regressing prompt-cache stability, redaction, or reverse-send guards.

options.title: Fold into structured handoff API work
options.body: Make https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/33478 the owner for typed delivery intent and close this only after that issue explicitly covers this WhatsApp acceptance case.

options.title: Use the open return-path PR
options.body: Continue review on https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/97311 or a repaired successor, then close this issue only after merged code proves the WhatsApp symptom fixed.

recommendation.title: Keep as WhatsApp acceptance work
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open until a narrow PR or repaired successor proves explicit WhatsApp source replies are delivered without regressing prompt-cache stability, redaction, or reverse-send guards.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest sessions_send delivery-semantics history and is already present in the issue timeline for this area.
